model.method: Multiplicative seasonal decomposition + OLS linear trend

base.label: Base case
base.description: Current 2025-26 run-rate continues: Mainland-led volume growth with gradual yield drift.
drivers: Segment spending mix held at 2025 levels

upside.label: Strategy delivered
upside.description: Strategic pillars land: more overnight, long-haul and MICE visitors lift yield.

downside.label: Headwinds
downside.description: Weaker regional demand, strong HKD and Mainland outbound diversion to other destinations.

pillars.title: High-Value, Long-Haul Experience & MICE Diversification
pillars.tagline: From same-day shopping to overnight, experience-driven stays
rationale: Same-day visitors account for 54.3% of 2026 YTD arrivals but spend HK$1,139 per head vs HK$5,503 for overnight visitors (2025).
Long-haul markets are only 7.4% of arrivals despite the highest per-capita spend.
Yield per visitor moved from HK$3,333 (2024) to HK$3,167 (2025) as volume shifted to same-day trips.
Singapore earned HK$11,578 per visitor in 2025 vs HK$3,167 for Hong Kong.
initiatives: Scale 'CityWalk' neighbourhood trails (Sham Shui Po, Sai Kung, Central-Western) into bookable multi-day itineraries.
Long-haul air-capacity incentives and stopover packages with airline partners through HKIA.
MICE bid fund targeting association congresses at AsiaWorld-Expo, HKCEC and Kai Tak.
Night-time economy and cultural districts (WestK, M+, Palace Museum) bundled as premium overnight products.

timeline.action: Launch long-haul stopover campaign and MICE bid fund round.
Roll out 10 bookable CityWalk itineraries with OTA partners.
Review overnight conversion and per-capita spend uplift.

pillars.title: Mega-Events & "+ Tourism" Integration
pillars.tagline: Kai Tak Sports Park as a year-round demand engine
rationale: Tourism, convention & exhibition BRI stood at 59.8 (2015 = 100) in 2026-Q2, up 3.8% YoY - still well below its 2015 base.
Accommodation receipts in Q4 run 34% above Q3 on average - events can fill the softer quarter.
Seasonal index ranges 0.81-1.22: events can fill the softer June and September troughs.
initiatives: Anchor a 12-month mega-event calendar at Kai Tak Sports Park (concerts, rugby sevens, e-sports).
'Sports + Tourism', 'Culture + Tourism' bundles: event ticket + hotel + attraction passes.
Target shoulder months (Jun, Sep) with signature festivals to smooth seasonality.
Event-impact dashboard tracking incremental arrivals, hotel nights and spend per event.

timeline.action: Lock 2027 Kai Tak anchor events and ticket-bundle partners.
Run shoulder-season festivals; publish per-event impact reports.

pillars.title: Seamless Cross-Boundary GBA Multi-Destination Strategy
pillars.tagline: Hong Kong as the international gateway to the Greater Bay Area
rationale: 76.1% of 2026 YTD visitor entries came via land, HSR or HZMB control points.
Mainland visitors make up 78.3% of 2026 YTD arrivals; most are same-day.
International visitors increasingly combine Hong Kong with Shenzhen, Macao and Guangzhou in one trip.
initiatives: Joint 'One Trip, Multiple Destinations' packages with Macao and GBA cities.
Single-ticketing across HSR, HZMB and ferries with integrated attraction passes.
Optimise transit visa and 144-hour visa-free routing for international visitors via HKIA.
Convert same-day Mainland flows into overnight stays with evening events and hotel bundles.

timeline.action: Launch single-ticket pilot (HSR + HZMB + attraction pass).
Extend transit-visa routing campaign to long-haul source markets.
